2026.PA18.2.t: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) Compliance
2026.PA18.2.s:

Management can confirm to the Board that the Toronto Parking Authority has successfully completed its Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) attestation of compliance as a Level 1 Merchant — the highest and most rigorous tier of Payment Card Industry compliance. This achievement affirms that Toronto Parking Authority’s payment infrastructure, information security controls, and operational governance across our GreenP Parking, Bike Share Toronto, and Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging operations meet the most demanding global standards for the protection of cardholder data.

The Toronto Parking Authority has now successfully achieved Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard attestation for six consecutive years of uninterrupted compliance. This sustained track record reflects managements continued efforts to maintain a culture of operating discipline, robust controls, and continuous improvements in our operating systems. This attestation is of strategic importance to the organization and is a foundational element of Toronto Parking Authority’s brand reputation in the marketplace. Our stewardship of consumer financial data information and security controls remains fundamental to our operating culture and commitment to our customers.

2026.PA19.4.t: Toronto Parking Authority - 2026 March 31 Year-to-Date Financial Performance (First Three Months Results)
2026.PA19.4.s:
Toronto Parking Authority's (TPA) operating income for the three months ended March 31, 2026, was $11.2 million; -$1.4 million versus plan and -$0.9 million versus 2025.

Total revenue was $37.6 million, -$2.4 million versus plan and -$1.4 million versus prior year, while total trip volumes were 5.7 million, -0.9 million versus plan and -0.6 million versus prior year. Negative performance driven by softness in our On-Street parking portfolio. On-Street revenue was $13.8 million, -$2.6 million versus plan due to 0.8 million fewer trips caused by winter storm closures. Excluding On-Street, top line revenue was +0.1 million better than plan and +$1.5 million versus 2025.

Total operating costs was $26.4 million; $0.9 million lower than plan driven by reduced volume-related costs, warranty cost reductions on legacy parking equipment, and head count savings.

As of March 31, 2026, Toronto Parking Authority has spent $3.9 million in capital projects, with another $34.2 million already committed. Building on the momentum from past three years of 80%+ spend rate, we are on track to deliver 95% or more of the Toronto Parking Authority led capital plan of $42.5 million.

Management is forecasting to deliver on plan full-year 2026 financial performance targets.
